svg.title: Rucio profiling and observability signal map
svg.desc: A comparison of CPU sampling, peak allocation, call statistics, Docker resources, and OpenTelemetry. Each view answers a different question and none attributes CPU, memory, and network usage to every method at once.
svg.text: Choose the signal that matches the question
Correlate views by workload and time; do not treat one profiler as complete attribution.

g.text: VIEW
CPU samples
Peak allocation
Call statistics
Container resources
Traces + logs
BEST QUESTION
Which Python stacks are on CPU?
Width is sample share, not chronology.
Which stacks contribute at high-water?
Allocation contribution is not retained memory.
Where is Python own/cumulative CPU time?
Deterministic instrumentation adds overhead.
When do containers use CPU, RAM, or I/O?
Panels auto-scale independently.
Where is elapsed latency across boundaries?
Spans show latency only where instrumented.
BOUNDARY / COMPLEMENT
No network bytes; native work can appear at its Python boundary.
Correlate with Docker CPU and a repeatable workload.
Not total container, PostgreSQL, or leak attribution.
Use child reports for forked processes and the memory timeline.
One process; threads included, spawned processes separate.
Confirm hotspots with statistical CPU sampling.
Whole-container counters; no per-method attribution.
Use JSONL deltas for exact sampled intervals.
Not CPU time; absence of a span is not absence of work.
Use trace IDs to move between Tempo and Loki.

svg.text: No supported view meters exact CPU, RAM, and network consumption for every Python method. Build a causal case from multiple signals.
